method: Stage attribution from read-only live-state inspection (curated review store, episode index, native search_memory_facts 24, get_episodes membership, resolver readback) plus the unmodified Central scorer. No raw facts or prompts.

live_state.cap_note: curatedRecallCandidates returns an empty inventory whenever eligible unique episodes exceed 288; 299>288 disabled the index for ALL 20 queries of this campaign.

indexed_only_loss.attribution: Expected episode absent from the native 24 and its curated index row ineligible because the whole inventory was disabled by the 288-episode cap. Not lexical preselection, not proof timeout, not dedup/budget: the inventory gate precedes all of them. Live source refs for these episodes are byte-identical to the frozen expectations (no source drift).

final_ranking_loss.attribution: Expected episode present in the native 24 (rank 10) and source-resolvable with the exact frozen ref; the presented set selected higher-ranked / near-duplicate facts in both strict (single-fact selector) and semantic (relative score threshold + near-duplicate dedup) modes.

unanchored_multi_event.attribution: Expected multi-event facts lost at INDEX_INVENTORY_CAP_EXCEEDED (index-only). Presented complementary facts were source-linked and anchored (query-lexeme overlap 1-4); no zero-lexeme unanchored fact was omitted by the one-fact cap because none reached the presented pool. Strict one-fact cap presented one complementary anchored fact; semantic presented up to 4 with near-duplicates of a single source.
